I'm 59, been farming these 18 mu in Quzhou since I was 14. Never went to school, but I know this land. My son works in a factory over in Shijiazhuang now, and my daughter-in-law has the grandkids to look after, so day-to-day it's mostly me and the old woman. That means we have to be careful with labor — I can't do the heavy work like I used to, and we don't have many hands at home.

**Wheat**: I got 10 mu of wheat in the ground now. Planted it October 12th last year, same week as always. I saved my own seed from the year before — been doing that for decades, no reason to pay the seed shop when my wheat grows fine. Cleaned it and treated it myself, cost almost nothing. Before planting I spread one big bag of that three-15 fertilizer for every two mu — so about 50 jin per mu. Then at jointing in early April I put down another 30 jin of urea per mu. Old Wang next door tried cutting back on fertilizer last year to save money, and his wheat turned yellow and thin. I'm not making that mistake — I'd rather waste a few yuan on extra fertilizer than lose half my crop. I already irrigated twice this spring, once at green-up and once at jointing. I'll water one more time when the heads come out in early May, then that's it. Pumping water costs too much to do more, and the wheat don't need it. For spraying, I did a herbicide right after planting, and I'll watch for rust or insects — if I see them, I'll spray, but I haven't needed much the last few years. I hire the combine for harvest in early June — costs about 60 yuan per mu, but it's the only way with just me and the wife. Should get around 800-900 jin per mu if the weather holds, same as most years.

**Maize**: After we cut the wheat, I got maybe 5 days to get the maize in — if you wait longer, the yield drops fast. I always buy hybrid seed from the shop, Zhengdan 958, everyone around here plants it. Costs about 45 yuan per mu. Can't save maize seed — tried that when I was young, the ears came out all scattered and small. I hire the tractor man to do quick rotary tilling right after the wheat comes off, then plant with the machine. Costs about 50 yuan per mu for the custom work, but it gets it in fast. I put compound fertilizer in the furrow when planting — about 40 jin per mu — then topdress with 20 jin of urea when the maize is knee-high, around mid-July. Irrigate once or twice in summer, depends on the rain. Last year was dry so I did two times, but some years one is enough. I don't spray much for maize — just one herbicide at planting. Should get around 900-1000 jin per mu.

**Cotton**: I'm putting 8 mu in cotton this year. Planted it April 15th, just last week. Used Bt cotton seed from the shop — costs about 50 yuan per mu, but it saves on bug spray. Before planting I plowed and made beds, then put down about 35 jin per mu of compound fertilizer mixed with 15 jin of urea in the soil. Cotton needs feeding. I'll irrigate three times — once now to get it started, once at flowering in July, and once in August if it's dry. The big worry is bollworm, even with Bt cotton. I'll spray for weeds right after planting, and probably spray for insects once in summer just to be safe. Cotton is the most work. Picking starts in September and goes to October, and with 8 mu we can't pick it all ourselves. Last year I hired women from the village — paid by the jin picked. Probably need 20-25 days of hired labor just for picking. Cotton prices have been okay though, so it's worth the trouble. Should get around 500-600 jin of seed cotton per mu, which is about what I always get.

**Money**: Everything costs more now. Fertilizer, diesel for the pump, hired labor for picking and harvest... I'm spending close to 10,000 yuan on inputs this year. That's a lot of money for me. But if I cut back too much, the yield drops and I lose more than I save. I've learned that the hard way. The wheat-maize gives steady grain and income, cotton gives cash. It's how we've always done it. I don't try anything fancy — I do what works, what my neighbors do, and what I can afford.
